title: Burak Çetin
text: 🚀 RapidPixel SDK v1.22.0 Update: Cross-Platform C++ SDK for Real-Time Video Processing Built with C++17, this toolkit provides ready-to-use components for developing real-time video processing and computer vision applications, including video capture, encoding and decoding, streaming, tracking, stabilization, object detection, video filtering, camera and lens control, communication, and other common video processing tasks. Instead of integrating many separate low-level libraries, developers can use larger, ready-made software building blocks and processing pipelines that are easy to integrate into their own applications. RapidPixel SDK supports Linux and Windows and runs on a wide range of platforms, including Intel, AMD, NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi, NXP i.MX8/i.MX9, Broadcom, Amlogic, and others. 🎥 Request a demo of RapidPixel SDK and see how it can accelerate your video processing development. #RapidPixel #ComputerVision #VideoProcessing #EmbeddedVision #CPlusPlus #EdgeAI #EmbeddedSystems

title: Low-altitude stability and propulsion responsiveness testing with SkyLane-350. Operating close to the ground provides a demanding environment to evaluate the aircraft’s hover stabi
text: Low-altitude stability and propulsion responsiveness testing with SkyLane-350. Operating close to the ground provides a demanding environment to evaluate the aircraft’s hover stability, control response and propulsion performance. During the test, we verify how quickly and precisely the propulsion system responds to flight controller commands while maintaining a stable position and altitude. These tests are an important part of validating the complete VTOL control loop - from sensors and flight control algorithms to motor response and propulsion dynamics. More info: https://lnkd.in/e_-wejbP #SkyDrones #SkyLane350 #VTOL #FlightTesting #FlightControl #Propulsion #UAV #AutonomousFlight

title: Priyam K.
text: The same conversation has come up more than once this year, and it always starts the same way, in my messages here. Someone in their early thirties who has taken over a family business. One version of them wants no part of what they inherited and is building something separate. Another is trying to take it to the moon. And a third doesnt know which way to turn. Different directions. Same question underneath. Which part of this is mine. They are usually moving quickly and have ambitious plans. What they have not checked is whose definition of winning they are running on. Most are a little annoyed when I ask. The idea is not to slow down. It is to make sure the direction is theirs before they spend another five years going that way at speed. If you recognised yourself somewhere in the last few weeks of posts, that is usually the signal. My messages are open.
author: Priyam K.

title: Rinata Ilyubayeva
text: Why did Network School choose Kazakhstan over 10+ countries? A new conversation with Balaji Srinivasan has just premiered across Trusted Kazakhstan, Astana Hub, and Network State Podcast. Network School is building a global community for people who want to learn tech, work remotely, build companies, and live alongside other ambitious people. Kazakhstan is set to become one of the first major global hubs for this model. In the conversation, Balaji Srinivasan, founder of Network School and former CTO of Coinbase, joins Rinata Ilyubayeva , Managing Director at Astana Hub, and host Thorsten Gutmann to discuss why Kazakhstan stood out among more than 10 countries considered for Network School’s expansion. The discussion goes beyond the decision itself. It explores: • why Astana can become a destination for global tech talent • how digital nomads can contribute to Kazakhstan’s innovation ecosystem • new approaches to education and lifelong learning • how global and local talent can build companies together • Kazakhstan’s growing focus on AI, emerging technologies, and new industries • what the cities and communities of the future could look like One of the central ideas of the conversation is simple: Kazakhstan has the opportunity not only to attract global talent, but to create an environment where people can build, scale, and take tech to international markets. For us at Astana Hub, this is also part of a broader ambition: to make Kazakhstan a place where international founders, engineers, creators, and investors can connect with local talent and build globally competitive tech businesses. Watch the full conversation: https://lnkd.in/eCDdXhGU Join Network School: https://ns.com/ Join the opening of Network School in Astana on September 2: https://luma.com/nskz Meet the global tech community at AI & Digital Bridge, October 1-3 in Astana: https://lnkd.in/d8j2HPmf
author: Rinata Ilyubayeva

title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D.
text: I’m excited to share that I’m starting a new role as Executive Technology Director, Advanced Research Office at GE Aerospace . As I make this transition, I’ve been reflecting on the past three years leading the Digital & Electrical Systems (DES) organization at the GE Aerospace Research Center. It has been a privilege to work with such a talented group of technology managers, researchers, and the broader research community across DES. I’m grateful to have been part of an organization that paired technical excellence with meaningful business outcomes. I’ve appreciated not only what the team accomplished, but how it was accomplished — through deep expertise, collaboration, innovation, and commitment. A special thank you to the DES management team — Kareem Aggour, Paul Ardis, David Esler, Denise Feirstein, John Garrity, Banu Gemici-Ozkan, Arun Gowda, Stacey Kennerly, and Eric Westervelt — for your leadership and partnership. I also want to recognize the broader research community that these leaders support every day; your contributions, creativity, and dedication have made a lasting impact. I’m proud of what we achieved together and excited for this next chapter in the Advanced Research Office.
author: Sachin Jain, Ph.D.
